children: DUG Technology
has increased revenue by 49% to US$34.4 million for the four months to 31 October 2026, supported by rapid growth in its computing, software, and Multi-Client businesses.
Contracted revenue climbed 52% to US$103.4m at 12 November from US$68m at the end of June, reflecting new commitments across its operating segments.
Multi-Client, Software, and high performance computing (HPC) collectively contributed 55% of sales, compared with 14% in the corresponding period last year.
The update, which comes ahead of the technology group’s annual general meeting on 19 November, highlights a changing revenue mix despite softer Services activity.
Computing and Software Growth
HPC revenue surged 715% to US$7.2m from US$0.9m, while Software revenue rose 84% to US$4m from US$2.2m.
Together, the two segments generated US$11.2m in revenue, representing a 266% increase on the comparable four-month period.
The group won US$43m of new committed HPC and Software contracts since 30 June, lifting combined contracted revenue in those businesses to US$67.6m.
Those commitments included awards of US$9.3m in August and US$33.7m in November, with the latter yet to generate a payment.
Multi-Client revenue reached US$7.6m against US$0.1m previously, with 12 projects now at varying stages of completion in its expanding library.
Customer Shift Underway
Services revenue declined 22% to US$15.6m from US$20m as some clients switched from outsourced processing to licensing DUG’s software and HPC capacity.
Other processing providers are using the same technology to compete for Services work, shifting revenue into DUG’s Software and HPC segments instead.
The company has begun converting its Services pipeline into active projects and expects that business to recover over the remainder of the financial year.
Services contracted revenue increased to US$35.8m at 12 November from US$33.6m at the end of June.
Multi-Client income is now disclosed separately, having previously been included within Services revenue, making the changing segment contributions more visible.
Earnings Margin Improves

EBITDA rose 45% to US$8.8m from US$6.1m, although its reported margin eased to 25.7% from 26.3%, while an 86% increase in normalised EBITDA to US$11.3m lifted the corresponding margin to 33% from 26.3%.
The normalised measure excludes US$2.5m of third-party cloud computing costs and is not calculated under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS).
“Our strategy of growing higher margin Multi-Client, Software, and HPC revenue is working, with more than half of our revenue now coming from these segments,” managing director Dr Matthew Lamont said
“It is especially exciting to see the Multi-Client business finding its feet—with US$103.4m of contracted revenue, we are well placed moving forward.”
Cash Position and Funding
Cash increased to US$17.7m at 12 November from US$10.5m at 30 June, while gross debt rose to US$30.4m from US$23.5m.
Net debt nevertheless edged down to US$12.7m from US$13m over the same period.
The higher gross debt reflects financing arranged after June for computing equipment delivered during the final week of that month and previously recorded in payables.
DUG separately acquired US$7m of additional computing equipment during the current financial year, funding those purchases from cash.
Management continues to review its debt profile while funding growth through existing cash reserves and operating cash flows.

title: DUG Technology Lifts Revenue 49% on Contracted Work Surge
